question_text: An announced investment at a summit should be treated as:

options.A: A policy or investor intention pending verification of actual deployment
options.B: Proof that all proposed jobs exist

option_assessment.A: Best answer: announcement is not itself evidence of completed deployment; no particular summit's conversion rate was established.
option_assessment.B: Incorrect: prospective employment does not establish filled jobs.
option_assessment.C: Incorrect: DPIIT separately measures actual FDI inflows (equity, reinvested earnings, other capital), not summit pledges.
option_assessment.D: Incorrect: a private investment announcement does not itself constitute a government budget appropriation.

primary_sources.title: Quarterly FDI Fact Sheet to June 2025
primary_sources.verified_scope: Published measurement of realised FDI inflows and components; does not directly audit summit announcements.

primary_sources.title: Foreign Investment Facilitation Portal
primary_sources.verified_scope: FDI proposal approvals are a separate administrative stage; does not establish deployment.

limitations: No particular summit MoU or project implementation record directly inspected.
No original budget appropriation law or labour employment dataset inspected; B/D rejected on logical category mismatch.
No PDF rendering or artifact verification performed after this evidence commit.
